# bce — the blueprint conformance engine

> A fail-closed architecture-conformance gate for AI-built systems. You author a blueprint (a durable
> architectural contract for a repository); bce measures the code against it and produces a
> deterministic conformance score, a fail-closed required-check gate for merges, and hash-chained
> evidence anyone can re-derive offline. Extraction is TypeScript/JavaScript today; the blueprint graph
> model is language-neutral, the extractor seam is documented, and Python is the named next community
> target. Status: v0.1.5 released with npm provenance; compatibility remains pre-1.0.

Core rules for an agent working in a bce-gated repo: (1) the gate is the done-check — a change is not
done until `bce gate` is green; (2) on a red, fix the code, never silently edit the blueprint; (3) the
baseline only ever shrinks — accepting a new violation is a reviewed human decision; (4) fail-closed,
no skip flags — a refusal is a red, not a pass.

## Start here

- [Quickstart (offline RED→fix→GREEN)](examples/quickstart/README.md): the guaranteed path, no API keys, five minutes.
- [Quickstart summary](docs/quickstart.md): the one-screen version.
- [First-win matrix](examples/first-win/README.md): the same loop on four starting shapes (empty repo, plain JavaScript, TypeScript, monorepo), each authoring its own contract with `bce author` and each wall-clock timed under 120s in CI.
- [Pick your shape](docs/first-win.md): which first-win walkthrough matches your repository, and the checkout-vs-published-package distinction.
- [README](README.md): what bce is, in a paragraph.

## Adoption

- [Adopt on an existing repo](docs/adopt-existing-repo.md): the ladder — advisory → baseline → graduate → enforced; the honest brownfield story.
- [FAQ](docs/faq.md): why baseline is not a bypass; why there is no skip flag.
- [Run bce in an agent loop](docs/agent-loop.md): per-harness (Claude Code / Cursor / generic MCP); the violation→fix→re-gate loop.
- [Integration snippets](integrations/README.md): drop-in CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / .cursorrules blocks + the MCP tools.
- [Agent Skill](skills/README.md): the full author → validate → run → teeth → gate lifecycle as a loadable skill; copy `skills/bce` into `.claude/skills/`.

## Reference

- [Specification](spec/SPEC.md): normative — artifact model, 11-type constraint taxonomy, scoring, modes, versioning.
- [Exit codes](docs/exit-codes.md): 0 = green, 1 = red/user-error, 2 = fail-closed refusal.
- [Report contract](docs/report-contract.md): the deterministic compliance report; determinism and canonical serialization.
- [Evidence format](docs/evidence-format.md): the hash-chained evidence record + the zero-dependency verifier.
- [Published schemas](spec/schemas): generated JSON Schemas (draft-07).
- [Conformance vectors](spec/conformance-vectors/README.md): input→expected-verdict data (no runner, no levels at v1alpha1).

## Authoring blueprints

- [Blueprint-author prompt pack (experimental)](prompts/blueprint-author.md): drive an agent to draft a blueprint from an existing repo; always ends in `bce teeth` + human review.
- [Prompt-pack validation](prompts/VALIDATION.md): the 5-public-repo acceptance runs.

## The engine gates itself

- [Self-hosting](docs/self-hosting.md): bce gates its own tree; Lane A/B, the bootstrap-0 exception, the Lane-A pin ceremony, the admin-override incident policy.
- [Corpus map](corpus/CORPUS-MAP.md): the seeded-defect corpus (recall denominator) and its relation to the paper corpus.
- [This repo's blueprint](.blueprints/engine.blueprint.json): the contract the self-gate enforces.
